top_news.title: DAMP: Decay-Aware Mixed-Precision Recurrent-State Quantization
top_news.dek: DAMP introduces post-training quantization for recurrent states in Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention to reduce memory usage and decoding latency.
top_news.brief: Recurrent states in models like GDN and KDA are typically stored in FP32, leading to high memory consumption and bandwidth bottlenecks. DAMP (Decay-Aware Mixed-Precision) addresses this by applying post-training quantization to these states, optimizing memory footprint without significantly sacrificing performance.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing recurrent state quantization process

top_news.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models
top_news.dek: Microsoft releases GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, optimized pathology foundation models for efficient large-scale analysis.
top_news.brief: What if pathology foundation models could do more with less? GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash cut computational demands while maintaining strong performance, opening the door to larger studies and broader exploration. The post GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models appeared first on Microsoft Research.

top_news.title: DoorDash’s Flux Runs 130,000 Engineering Tasks Through Cloud-Based Agents
top_news.dek: DoorDash has migrated its engineering agent workloads to a cloud-based platform called Flux, automating 130,000 tasks in a single month.
top_news.brief: Flux moves agent execution from local developer machines to a centralized cloud environment using Firecracker microVMs. The platform supports over 25,000 automated code reviews weekly, utilizing an MCP gateway and reusable playbooks to ensure scoped access and consistent auditing across engineering workflows.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing agentic workflows moving from local laptops to a secure cloud-based microVM architecture.

top_news.title: Browser Run - Crawl endpoint now respects the Content Signals `use` directive
top_news.dek: Cloudflare's /crawl endpoint now supports the Content Signals 'use' directive to respect site owner preferences for AI training data usage.
top_news.brief: Developers can now specify a 'contentUse' parameter, with options for 'reference' or 'full' access. If a target site's robots.txt defines a 'use' level more restrictive than the requested parameter, the crawl request will return a 400 error, enforcing compliance with site-level data usage policies.
top_news.image_alt: Code snippet demonstrating the new contentUse parameter in a curl request.

top_news.title: Run NVIDIA BioNeMo NIM Microservices for Protein Structure Prediction in Claude Science
top_news.dek: NVIDIA has integrated BioNeMo NIM microservices with Claude Science to enable agentic workflows for protein structure prediction.
top_news.brief: The integration allows AI agents to perform iterative scientific research by calling domain-specific models directly. By leveraging BioNeMo NIMs, researchers can automate the process of folding proteins and characterizing molecules, moving beyond simple code generation into complex, iterative scientific experimentation.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual workflow of an AI agent interacting with BioNeMo NIM microservices for scientific research.

primary.title: DAMP: Decay-Aware Mixed-Precision Recurrent-State Quantization
primary.summary: Softmax attention stores key and value vectors for every preceding token, causing inference memory to grow with sequence length. Recent language models incorporating Gated DeltaNet (GDN) or Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) reduce this cost by replacing the KV cache in most layers with fixed-size recurrent states. However, these recurrent states are commonly stored in FP32 and consume substantial GPU memory; their updates are memory-bandwidth bound and contribute significantly to decoding latency. To our knowledge, we are the first to study post-training quantization of recurrent states in GDN and KD

primary.title: Marginal Coverage Credit Reduces Redundant Exploration in Parallel State-Entropy Optimization
primary.summary: Policy Gradient for Parallel State Entropy maximization (PGPSE) expands state-space coverage by training independently parameterized policies in replicated copies of the same environment. However, its pooled team-entropy score measures only collective exploration and cannot identify policies that contribute non-redundant coverage. We introduce Marginal Coverage Credit for PGPSE (MCC-PGPSE), which combines leave-one-policy-out coverage with state-owner specialization to estimate policy-specific credit. MCC-PGPSE preserves PGPSE's pooled objective and redistributes non-negative auxiliary intrins
